Post-burn residue and ash from a controlled test burn are digested and analysed in addition to the unburnt article, because combustion concentrates non-volatile metal rather than destroying it. In addition, REACH Annex XVII entry 20 compliance is a MANDATORY PRECONDITION and is verified by organotin speciation (GC-MS or GC-ICP-MS for dibutyltin, dioctyltin, tributyltin and triphenyltin) on every elastomer, gasket, liner, seal and silicone component: an article supplied to the general public in which organotin expressed as tin exceeds 0.1 percent by weight is unlawful in the European Union and that finding blocks certification outright, independently of the total-tin result. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the wax supplier, fragrance house, dye or pigment supplier, wick supplier and vessel or decorator supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

control.rationale: No government sets an aluminium content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. The aluminium instruments on the register were checked and each fails on basis or on route: the EU Toy Safety Directive aluminium values are EN 71-3 element migration limits from toy material, and the dietary and food-additive aluminium provisions are calibrated to oral intake and oral absorption. Aluminium is also the panel analyte for which route-transfer is least defensible in principle, because a dietary aluminium limit is written against gastrointestinal absorption of well under one percent, which does not describe deposition in the respiratory tract. HMTc states that asymmetry and does NOT convert it into a number: no exposure model, no percentile and no precautionary adjustment produces a value here, and none of the route-scoped inhaled-product instruments publishes aluminium at all. A not-material determination is rejected: Aluminium is material here: aluminium vessels and lids, aluminium-pigment decorative lustres and metallic finishes, and aluminosilicate or kaolin wax fillers, all of which report to the ash and residue when the candle burns down. The cell is a control. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
control.reference_method: Aluminium on every certified lot of the unburnt wax-and-fragrance body, sampled through its full depth by microwave-assisted acid digestion, using a hydrofluoric or tetrafluoroboric acid step wherever an aluminosilicate mineral phase is present (a nitric-only digest does not liberate aluminium bound in clay, kaolin, talc or zeolite and will under-report it by an order of magnitude), followed by ICP-MS or ICP-OES. Component-level sampling covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm, beeswax or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any mineral or polymer hardener, opacifier or UV stabiliser; the wick, its core, sustainer tab and adhesive; the glass, ceramic, tinplate or aluminium vessel and any glaze, enamel, lustre, decal or metallic surface coating; and the lid, with aluminium primary packaging, foil seals, metallised decoration and aluminosilicate fillers reported separately from the emitting mass. Post-burn residue and ash from a controlled test burn are digested and analysed in addition to the unburnt article, because combustion concentrates non-volatile metal rather than destroying it. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the wax supplier, fragrance house, dye or pigment supplier, wick supplier and vessel or decorator supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

control.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel screen number in this programme; it is the toxic species reached by reflex speciation from total chromium. No government sets a hexavalent-chromium content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product: Maryland publishes plain total chromium for the inhalation route and does not speciate, and no other route-scoped instrument publishes chromium in any form. The nearest hexavalent-chromium instruments were checked and each fails on basis or on scope: EU RoHS (0.1 percent by weight in the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment), REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 (1 mg/kg after extraction in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles), REACH entry 47 for leather articles, the EU Toy Safety Directive EN 71-3 migration limits, and drinking-water maximum contaminant levels expressed per litre. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other. A not-material determination is rejected: Chromium is material here and specifically so for a combustion form: chromium in wick supports, chrome-bearing pigments, mordants and glaze frits can be oxidised from the trivalent to the hexavalent state at flame and glow temperatures, and inhaled hexavalent chromium is a Group 1 respiratory carcinogen. The cell is a control with reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
control.reference_method: Total chromium on every certified lot of the unburnt wax-and-fragrance body, sampled through its full depth by digestion and ICP-MS, read against the published total-chromium SCREEN of 600 ug/kg. Reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation by EPA 3060A alkaline extraction with EPA 6800 isotope-dilution IC-ICP-MS, or by EN 15192, is ordered whenever total chromium reaches half the screen (300 ug/kg), unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier of plated, passivated, glazed, enamelled, mordanted or chrome-pigmented component, and unconditionally on every lot of a combustion or heated form. On combustion and heated forms speciation is performed on the post-burn residue and ash, or on the reservoir residue film, as well as on the unburnt article, because glow, flame and sustained melt-pool temperatures oxidise trivalent chromium to the hexavalent state. Component-level sampling covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm, beeswax or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any mineral or polymer hardener, opacifier or UV stabiliser; the wick, its core, sustainer tab and adhesive; the glass, ceramic, tinplate or aluminium vessel and any glaze, enamel, lustre, decal or metallic surface coating; and the lid. DISPOSITION: any hexavalent chromium quantifiable above the method limit of quantitation fails the lot. Inhaled hexavalent chromium is a Group 1 respiratory carcinogen and the programme publishes no permissible level for it; the total-chromium screen is the tripwire, not the ceiling. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the wax supplier, fragrance house, dye or pigment supplier, wick supplier and vessel or decorator supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. This row's emitting material is a manufactured non-marine formulation (the unburnt wax-and-fragrance body, sampled through its full depth) with no methylation pathway, no aquatic trophic transfer and no marine-derived or wild-harvested animal input, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so MeHg is less than or equal to tHg by identity and is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury ceiling of 100 ug/kg. Methylmercury is additionally thermally labile and decomposes well below the temperatures reached in any heated or combustion form in this category, so no thermal pathway creates it either. No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury limit for any air-care product, and no routed occurrence source reports methylmercury in one, which is the speciation-aware condition the not-material integrity gate applies. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling.
not_material.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell, which is determined on every lot by EPA 7473 thermal decomposition/amalgamation atomic absorption or by ICP-MS after closed-vessel digestion. Methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total mercury reaches half the published total-mercury ceiling (50 ug/kg), or where a reformulation introduces any marine-derived, fish-derived or wild-harvested animal raw material, which would additionally require the row to be re-dispositioned from not-material to control.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for an air freshener, evaporator, puff releaser, candle, wax melt, diffuser, incense, potpourri, vacuum fragrance additive or fragrance refill. Every methylmercury instrument on the register is scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, EU Regulation (EU) 2022/617, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Thailand MOPH 414, Vietnam QCVN 8-2, Philippines PNS/BAFS 194, Mexico NOM-242, GSO 193, Trinidad and Tobago). Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically cannot exceed, total mercury, which this row publishes at 100 ug/kg by disclosed read-across from the Colorado inhalation-route maximum.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: Route-scoped inhaled-product instruments: Colorado MED 2022, California DCC section 15723, Maryland Cannabis Administration Rev. 6.0, Massachusetts CCC 2020, Nevada CCB 2020, Israel MoH IMC-GMP 152 - none publishes methylmercury. Article and component instruments: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU, EU Batteries Regulation Annex I, REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23, 63 and 72, Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2018-83, Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892, EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, US 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) - none publishes methylmercury. Cosmetic instruments: Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, ASEAN Cosmetic Directive v3 2019, Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9, China CSAR 2015, India Cosmetics Rules 2020, Indonesia BPOM 16/2024, Malaysia NPRA, New Zealand Group Standard, Kenya KS 2937:2021, Taiwan 2024, EAEU TR CU 009/2011, Hong Kong Mercury Control Ordinance - all regulate total mercury only. Dietary methylmercury instruments are fish-scoped and excluded by applicability.

scented-candles.material: the unburnt wax-and-fragrance body (wax base, fragrance load, dye or pigment and any hardener, opacifier or stabiliser), burnt through a wick in a glass, ceramic, tinplate or aluminium vessel
scented-candles.components: The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm, beeswax or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any mineral or polymer hardener, opacifier or UV stabiliser; the wick, its core, sustainer tab and adhesive; the glass, ceramic, tinplate or aluminium vessel and any glaze, enamel, lustre, decal or metallic surface coating; and the lid. Every listed component is sampled and tested as a distinct component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, and hexavalent-chromium reflex speciation on a component follows the reference method published on this row's Cr-VI cell. Beyond the components, the post-burn residue and ash are recovered and analysed as a separate matrix. EMISSION PATH. The components in the emission path, which branch (b) of every numeric cell's disposition governs, are the wick with its core, sustainer tab and adhesive, and the inner surface of the vessel with any glaze, enamel, lustre or coating on it that the molten pool wets. Every component result carries a criterion and a lot consequence under the three ordered branches published on each numeric cell: a sovereign instrument that reaches the component and the analyte governs it in its own basis and an exceedance blocks certification; an emission-path component is governed through the published value applied to emitting material sampled from the finished assembled article; and any remaining component result is held to ALARA against demonstrated process capability, with CAPA, raw-material traceback and a block on certification where an uncontrolled source is confirmed. No component ceiling is invented.

scented-wax-blocks-melts.name: Scented wax blocks/wax melts
scented-wax-blocks-melts.native_basis_label: as sold, micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material (the fragrance concentrate, wax, gel, botanical mass or refill charge that is aerosolised, evaporated or combusted), with component-level screening of the article's non-emitting parts; a content screen on the article and its refill, never an emission rate, a per-actuation dose or an indoor-air concentration
scented-wax-blocks-melts.scope_note: FORM AND EMISSION MECHANISM. A wickless wax block, bar, cube or shaped melt is placed in a separate electric or tealight-heated warmer and the fragrance evaporates from an open melt pool held near or above its flash point for hours. Because the article carries no wick of its own, the United States and Australian lead-cored-wick prohibitions do not reach it: the heat source is a separate product. That limitation is stated here rather than glossed over. SCOPE. In scope: wickless scented wax melts, cubes, bars, blocks, shapes and brittle in clamshells or wrapped presentations. Out of scope: the warmers themselves, wick-bearing tealights supplied to heat them (which route to the scented-candles row), and wax-based cosmetic or depilatory products. Note for the certificate and for consumer-facing labelling: wax melts are routinely moulded, coloured and scented to resemble confectionery and are a documented paediatric ingestion hazard; that is a product-design and labelling finding recorded at Step 0, not a basis for importing a dietary or mouthable-article limit into this row. COMPONENTS SAMPLED. The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any hardener, opacifier, glitter or mica-effect additive; embedded botanical or mineral inclusions; and the clamshell, tray or film packaging in direct contact with the wax. BASIS, AND WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT MEASURE. The panel is a CONTENT SCREEN on the article and on its refill, expressed in micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material. It is not an inhalation exposure limit, not an emission-rate limit, not a per-actuation or per-hour dose limit, and not an indoor-air concentration limit, and it must not be presented as any of those. No credible sovereign government sets an inhalation exposure limit for these metals in a consumer air product, and HMTc does not manufacture one: no occupational exposure limit and no ambient- or indoor-air guideline is converted into a product ceiling anywhere in this category. Because this form works by heating and evaporation, the content screen is a LOWER BOUND on what the emission path can carry: driving off the volatile fraction concentrates non-volatile metal in the reservoir, wick tip or residue film across repeated use, so residue analysis is mandatory alongside the charge as supplied. ROUTING. Placement in this category follows the taxonomy boundary rules: the primary exposure pathway must be inhalation or ambient-air emission; an essential oil sold as aromatherapy for diffusion routes here, the same oil sold as a topical leave-on skin product routes to Category 13 and sold as a dietary supplement routes to Category 16; and marketing and positioning decide routing where one formulation could serve several functions.
scented-wax-blocks-melts.audit_exclude_scope: non.inhalable|oral route|cutaneous route|edible cannabis|oral consumption|rectal or vaginal|topical|transdermal|drinking water|water intended|bottled|mineral water|public water systems|jewel|\btoy|infant|baby|toddler|\bfeed\b|fertilis|fertiliz|sewage|biosolid|growing media|cosmetic|makeup|make-up|tattoo|eraser
scented-wax-blocks-melts.basis_guard_note: Category 22 numeric cells are anchored ONLY in route-scoped inhaled-product content instruments, whose register basis strings are "product as tested" (Colorado, Maryland) and "cannabis or cannabis product" (California). The guard admits exactly those and rejects, by construction, every other basis family the register carries: dietary wet-weight maximum levels (an ingestion basis), food-contact and toy element-migration limits (a leachate basis), RoHS and REACH percent-by-weight restrictions on homogeneous materials, plastics, paints and batteries (an end-of-life materials basis), surface-coating dried-film limits, drinking-water statutory limits (a per-litre basis), cosmetic technically-avoidable trace limits (a dermal basis), colour-additive purity specifications, feed 12-percent-moisture bases, and the candlewick prohibition threshold, which is expressed on the mass of the metal in the wick core and not on any product. A number in the wrong basis is not a maximum level for this product form and must never anchor a row here.

read_across.label: read-across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division route-scoped maximum for inhaled product and metered-dose nasal spray (500 ug/kg), corroborated at the identical value by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products
read_across.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a lead content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 500 ug/kg, from Colorado (co2022 inhaled/nasal row). California DCC section 15723 independently sets the identical 0.5 ug/g for inhalable products (us_ca_dcc_2026_pb_inhalable_cannabis_0_5ugg), so two sub-national regulators converge on this value. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: Maryland inhalation route 1000 ug/kg, Massachusetts all-uses protocol 500 ug/kg (equal but route-unspecific), Nevada 1200 ug/kg, Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 5000 ug/kg. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the unburnt wax melt body, sampled across the full block or across a representative set of cubes by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. DISPOSITION OF THE ADDITIONAL ANALYSES THIS CELL MANDATES. This cell requires one analysis beyond the published test, and it carries a criterion and a lot consequence, so that no mandatory analysis on this row is an obligation without an outcome. COMPONENT RESULTS, THE FIRST ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The published ceiling of 500 ug/kg governs the emitting material and is NOT transferred to a component's bulk content: a metallic-effect glitter or mica additive, an embedded mineral inclusion, or a metallised clamshell, tray or film is or may be substantially metal, metal-plated, metal-glazed or metal-pigmented by construction, and reading an emitting-material value against a structural component's bulk content would be exactly the basis conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent, failing every compliant article for a metal that never enters the air. Every component result is instead dispositioned in three ordered branches, and no component result is left outside them. (a) WHERE A SOVEREIGN INSTRUMENT REACHES THE COMPONENT AND THIS ANALYTE, that instrument is the criterion. For lead and this row's components, branch (a) is EMPTY, and the instruments checked before saying so are named rather than waved at: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU is scoped to the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment and this row carries no powered sub-assembly; Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries is scoped to batteries and this row contains none; REACH Annex XVII entry 63 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2015/628 (eu_2015_628_pb_mouthable_general_public_articles_0_05pct) reaches only articles supplied to the general public that may be placed in the mouth by children; Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 reaches consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles and does not reach a packaging, sachet or decorative textile that is not worn; the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, the CPSIA surface-coating limit and the Canadian and Australian toy-coating limits reach accessible toy material and toy surface coatings, and none of these articles is a toy; 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) reaches only the metal of a candlewick core and this row has no wick core; the food-contact ceramic, glassware and enamelware instruments reach only articles intended to come into contact with food. Every component result on this row therefore falls to branch (b) or branch (c), and neither leaves a result without a criterion or without a lot consequence. (b) WHERE THE COMPONENT IS IN THE EMISSION PATH (the clamshell, tray or film in direct contact with the wax, and any embedded botanical or mineral inclusion that melts with it), the criterion is the published ceiling itself, applied where its basis makes it meaningful: the test is performed on emitting material sampled from the finished, filled and assembled article rather than from a pre-fill bulk batch, at the end of the declared shelf life or after the declared maximum melt cycle in the warmer the manufacturer specifies, whichever is the more demanding, so that any lead transferred out of an emission-path component into the emitting material is carried into the published result rather than escaping it. An emitting-material result at or above 500 ug/kg fails the lot. A rising component result while the emitting material stays below the ceiling does not by itself fail the lot and falls to branch (c). (c) OTHERWISE, for a component outside the emission path that no sovereign instrument reaches for lead, the component result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule, in the same terms this row's control cells already use: the result is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the wax refiner, the fragrance house, the dye or pigment and effect-additive supplier, the inclusion supplier and the packaging converter; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row. No component ceiling is invented in branch (c), because no credible sovereign government publishes a lead content maximum for these components in this product form, and an occupational exposure limit, an indoor-air guideline and an ambient-air standard are none of them converted into one.

control.rationale: No government sets an inorganic-arsenic content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. Every route-scoped inhaled-product instrument regulates arsenic as the unspeciated total: Colorado, California, Maryland, Massachusetts, Nevada and Israel all publish total arsenic and none of them speciates, so there is no inorganic-arsenic cell anywhere to read across from. The article and component instruments checked were EU RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU Annex II (lead, cadmium, total mercury and hexavalent chromium in the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment), the EU Batteries Regulation Annex I (mercury, cadmium and lead in batteries), REACH Annex XVII entry 23 (cadmium in synthetic polymers, paint and painted articles), REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin expressed as tin in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public), REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and hexavalent chromium in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles), REACH Annex XVII entry 63 paragraph 7 (lead in mouthable articles), Canada SOR/2016-193 (lead and mercury in surface coating materials), Canada SOR/2018-83 (lead in accessible parts of children's products), Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892 (lead and cadmium in listed covered consumer products), and the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 with EN 71-3 (element migration from toy materials). Every one of them governs a component of an article in a different basis, and none of them is a content maximum for the material a home-air product puts into the breathing zone. The cosmetic content instruments checked and rejected on route were Germany BVL 2017 (technically avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics), Health Canada's cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits, the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive contaminant guideline v3 (2019), Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9, China's 2015 Cosmetics Safety and Technical Standards, India's Cosmetics Rules 2020, Indonesia BPOM 16/2024, Malaysia NPRA, the New Zealand Cosmetic Products Group Standard, Kenya KS 2937:2021, Taiwan's 2024 prohibited-ingredient residual limits, EAEU TR CU 009/2011, and the Hong Kong Mercury Control Ordinance cosmetics provision. All of them are content limits for products applied to the human body on a dermal or mucosal basis. A home-air product is not applied to the body, so none of them is route-applicable. A NOT-MATERIAL determination is deliberately rejected rather than adopted for convenience, because inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction and it is genuinely material in this row. Inorganic arsenic is material here through mineral pigments, mica and clay-derived effect additives and fillers. The cell is therefore a control: testing is mandatory, the species is bounded by identity below the published total-arsenic ceiling of 200 ug/kg, and no number is invented. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
control.reference_method: Total arsenic on every certified lot of the unburnt wax melt body, sampled across the full block or across a representative set of cubes by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the ArCl interference. Reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS is ordered whenever the total-arsenic screen reaches half the published total-arsenic ceiling (100 ug/kg), and unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier of mineral filler, pigment, glaze, frit, clay, charcoal, joss powder, hydrocolloid or dried botanical material. Component-level sampling covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any hardener, opacifier, glitter or mica-effect additive; embedded botanical or mineral inclusions; and the clamshell, tray or film packaging in direct contact with the wax. The residue film recovered from the reservoir, dish or wick tip after a controlled heating cycle is analysed in addition to the charge as supplied. Because inorganic arsenic is a fraction of total arsenic, a lot in which inorganic arsenic alone reaches 200 ug/kg also fails the published total-arsenic ceiling. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the wax supplier, fragrance house, dye or pigment supplier and any inclusion or effect-additive supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

control.rationale: No government sets a nickel content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. Every route-scoped inhaled-product instrument on the register omits nickel entirely, including Maryland's inhalation-route table, which publishes lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium and total chromium but no nickel. The nearest nickel instruments were checked and each fails on basis or on route: the EU Toy Safety Directive nickel values are element MIGRATION limits from toy material under EN 71-3, not content limits; REACH Annex XVII entry 27 governs nickel RELEASE RATE from skin-piercing and prolonged-skin-contact articles; Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9 set nickel content limits for cosmetics on a dermal basis; and EU Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 sets dietary nickel maximum levels on an ingestion basis. No conversion between a migration limit, a release rate, a dermal cosmetic limit and a total-content limit for an inhaled product is defensible, and none is performed. A not-material determination is rejected: Nickel is material here: nickel-bearing pigments and mica-effect and glitter additives are common in this form, and repeated melt-and-solidify cycles concentrate non-volatile additives in the residue left in the warmer dish. The cell is a control. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
control.reference_method: Nickel on every certified lot of the unburnt wax melt body, sampled across the full block or across a representative set of cubes by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with collision/reaction-cell control of the CaO and ArNa interferences. Component-level sampling covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any hardener, opacifier, glitter or mica-effect additive; embedded botanical or mineral inclusions; and the clamshell, tray or film packaging in direct contact with the wax, with every nickel-plated, nickel-alloy and stainless component in the emission path digested and reported separately rather than averaged into the article mass. The residue film recovered from the reservoir, dish or wick tip after a controlled heating cycle is analysed in addition to the charge as supplied. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the wax supplier, fragrance house, dye or pigment supplier and any inclusion or effect-additive supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

control.rationale: No government sets a total-tin content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. The tin instruments on the register were checked and each fails on basis or on scope: the Codex, EU, Hong Kong and Japan canned-food tin maximum levels govern tin dissolved from tinplate INTO A FOOD on a dietary as-consumed basis; the EU Toy Safety Directive tin values are EN 71-3 migration limits from toy material; and REACH Annex XVII entry 20 restricts ORGANOTIN SPECIES expressed as tin in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public, which does directly cover the articles in this row but is a species restriction at 0.1 percent by weight rather than a total-tin content ceiling, and adopting 1,000,000 ug/kg as this row's tin limit would be to publish a number that protects nobody. It is recorded as the companion instrument and enforced as a precondition instead. A not-material determination is rejected: Tin is material here: tin-bearing stabilisers in polymer and glitter additives, and tinplate or metallised packaging in direct wax contact. The cell is a control. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
control.reference_method: Total tin on every certified lot of the unburnt wax melt body, sampled across the full block or across a representative set of cubes by microwave-assisted acid digestion in an HCl-containing matrix (tin is readily lost by hydrolysis and precipitation from a nitric-only digest) and ICP-MS. Component-level sampling covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any hardener, opacifier, glitter or mica-effect additive; embedded botanical or mineral inclusions; and the clamshell, tray or film packaging in direct contact with the wax, with tinplate, solder and metallised components reported separately. The residue film recovered from the reservoir, dish or wick tip after a controlled heating cycle is analysed in addition to the charge as supplied. In addition, REACH Annex XVII entry 20 compliance is a MANDATORY PRECONDITION and is verified by organotin speciation (GC-MS or GC-ICP-MS for dibutyltin, dioctyltin, tributyltin and triphenyltin) on every elastomer, gasket, liner, seal and silicone component: an article supplied to the general public in which organotin expressed as tin exceeds 0.1 percent by weight is unlawful in the European Union and that finding blocks certification outright, independently of the total-tin result. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the wax supplier, fragrance house, dye or pigment supplier and any inclusion or effect-additive supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

control.rationale: No government sets an aluminium content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. The aluminium instruments on the register were checked and each fails on basis or on route: the EU Toy Safety Directive aluminium values are EN 71-3 element migration limits from toy material, and the dietary and food-additive aluminium provisions are calibrated to oral intake and oral absorption. Aluminium is also the panel analyte for which route-transfer is least defensible in principle, because a dietary aluminium limit is written against gastrointestinal absorption of well under one percent, which does not describe deposition in the respiratory tract. HMTc states that asymmetry and does NOT convert it into a number: no exposure model, no percentile and no precautionary adjustment produces a value here, and none of the route-scoped inhaled-product instruments publishes aluminium at all. A not-material determination is rejected: Aluminium is material here: aluminium-pigment lustres, mica and aluminosilicate effect additives, aluminium foil and metallised film packaging in direct contact with the wax, and kaolin wax fillers. The cell is a control. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
control.reference_method: Aluminium on every certified lot of the unburnt wax melt body, sampled across the full block or across a representative set of cubes by microwave-assisted acid digestion, using a hydrofluoric or tetrafluoroboric acid step wherever an aluminosilicate mineral phase is present (a nitric-only digest does not liberate aluminium bound in clay, kaolin, talc or zeolite and will under-report it by an order of magnitude), followed by ICP-MS or ICP-OES. Component-level sampling covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any hardener, opacifier, glitter or mica-effect additive; embedded botanical or mineral inclusions; and the clamshell, tray or film packaging in direct contact with the wax, with aluminium primary packaging, foil seals, metallised decoration and aluminosilicate fillers reported separately from the emitting mass. The residue film recovered from the reservoir, dish or wick tip after a controlled heating cycle is analysed in addition to the charge as supplied. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the wax supplier, fragrance house, dye or pigment supplier and any inclusion or effect-additive supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

control.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel screen number in this programme; it is the toxic species reached by reflex speciation from total chromium. No government sets a hexavalent-chromium content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product: Maryland publishes plain total chromium for the inhalation route and does not speciate, and no other route-scoped instrument publishes chromium in any form. The nearest hexavalent-chromium instruments were checked and each fails on basis or on scope: EU RoHS (0.1 percent by weight in the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment), REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 (1 mg/kg after extraction in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles), REACH entry 47 for leather articles, the EU Toy Safety Directive EN 71-3 migration limits, and drinking-water maximum contaminant levels expressed per litre. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other. A not-material determination is rejected: Chromium is material here: chrome-bearing pigments are used to obtain saturated colours in this form, and the melt pool is held hot for hours in an open dish where oxidation of trivalent to hexavalent chromium in the residue cannot be ruled out. The cell is a control with reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
control.reference_method: Total chromium on every certified lot of the unburnt wax melt body, sampled across the full block or across a representative set of cubes by digestion and ICP-MS, read against the published total-chromium SCREEN of 600 ug/kg. Reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation by EPA 3060A alkaline extraction with EPA 6800 isotope-dilution IC-ICP-MS, or by EN 15192, is ordered whenever total chromium reaches half the screen (300 ug/kg), unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier of plated, passivated, glazed, enamelled, mordanted or chrome-pigmented component, and unconditionally on every lot of a combustion or heated form. On combustion and heated forms speciation is performed on the post-burn residue and ash, or on the reservoir residue film, as well as on the unburnt article, because glow, flame and sustained melt-pool temperatures oxidise trivalent chromium to the hexavalent state. Component-level sampling covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any hardener, opacifier, glitter or mica-effect additive; embedded botanical or mineral inclusions; and the clamshell, tray or film packaging in direct contact with the wax. DISPOSITION: any hexavalent chromium quantifiable above the method limit of quantitation fails the lot. Inhaled hexavalent chromium is a Group 1 respiratory carcinogen and the programme publishes no permissible level for it; the total-chromium screen is the tripwire, not the ceiling. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the wax supplier, fragrance house, dye or pigment supplier and any inclusion or effect-additive supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. This row's emitting material is a manufactured non-marine formulation (the unburnt wax melt body, sampled across the full block or across a representative set of cubes) with no methylation pathway, no aquatic trophic transfer and no marine-derived or wild-harvested animal input, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so MeHg is less than or equal to tHg by identity and is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury ceiling of 100 ug/kg. Methylmercury is additionally thermally labile and decomposes well below the temperatures reached in any heated or combustion form in this category, so no thermal pathway creates it either. No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury limit for any air-care product, and no routed occurrence source reports methylmercury in one, which is the speciation-aware condition the not-material integrity gate applies. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling.
not_material.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell, which is determined on every lot by EPA 7473 thermal decomposition/amalgamation atomic absorption or by ICP-MS after closed-vessel digestion. Methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total mercury reaches half the published total-mercury ceiling (50 ug/kg), or where a reformulation introduces any marine-derived, fish-derived or wild-harvested animal raw material, which would additionally require the row to be re-dispositioned from not-material to control.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for an air freshener, evaporator, puff releaser, candle, wax melt, diffuser, incense, potpourri, vacuum fragrance additive or fragrance refill. Every methylmercury instrument on the register is scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, EU Regulation (EU) 2022/617, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Thailand MOPH 414, Vietnam QCVN 8-2, Philippines PNS/BAFS 194, Mexico NOM-242, GSO 193, Trinidad and Tobago). Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically cannot exceed, total mercury, which this row publishes at 100 ug/kg by disclosed read-across from the Colorado inhalation-route maximum.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: Route-scoped inhaled-product instruments: Colorado MED 2022, California DCC section 15723, Maryland Cannabis Administration Rev. 6.0, Massachusetts CCC 2020, Nevada CCB 2020, Israel MoH IMC-GMP 152 - none publishes methylmercury. Article and component instruments: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU, EU Batteries Regulation Annex I, REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23, 63 and 72, Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2018-83, Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892, EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, US 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) - none publishes methylmercury. Cosmetic instruments: Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, ASEAN Cosmetic Directive v3 2019, Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9, China CSAR 2015, India Cosmetics Rules 2020, Indonesia BPOM 16/2024, Malaysia NPRA, New Zealand Group Standard, Kenya KS 2937:2021, Taiwan 2024, EAEU TR CU 009/2011, Hong Kong Mercury Control Ordinance - all regulate total mercury only. Dietary methylmercury instruments are fish-scoped and excluded by applicability.

scented-wax-blocks-melts.material: the unburnt wax melt body (wax base, fragrance load, dye or pigment and any effect additive or inclusion), melted without a wick in a separately supplied warmer
scented-wax-blocks-melts.components: The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any hardener, opacifier, glitter or mica-effect additive; embedded botanical or mineral inclusions; and the clamshell, tray or film packaging in direct contact with the wax. Every listed component is sampled and tested as a distinct component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, and hexavalent-chromium reflex speciation on a component follows the reference method published on this row's Cr-VI cell. EMISSION PATH. The components in the emission path, which branch (b) of every numeric cell's disposition governs, are the clamshell, tray or film in direct contact with the wax, and any embedded botanical or mineral inclusion that melts with it. Every component result carries a criterion and a lot consequence under the three ordered branches published on each numeric cell: a sovereign instrument that reaches the component and the analyte governs it in its own basis and an exceedance blocks certification; an emission-path component is governed through the published value applied to emitting material sampled from the finished assembled article; and any remaining component result is held to ALARA against demonstrated process capability, with CAPA, raw-material traceback and a block on certification where an uncontrolled source is confirmed. No component ceiling is invented.

heated-oil-diffusers.name: Heated oil diffusers
heated-oil-diffusers.native_basis_label: as sold, micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material (the fragrance concentrate, wax, gel, botanical mass or refill charge that is aerosolised, evaporated or combusted), with component-level screening of the article's non-emitting parts; a content screen on the article and its refill, never an emission rate, a per-actuation dose or an indoor-air concentration
heated-oil-diffusers.scope_note: FORM AND EMISSION MECHANISM. A heated reservoir, powered by mains, USB or a tealight, raises an essential-oil or fragrance-oil charge, sometimes floated on a water bath, to the point of rapid evaporation. Heating an oil drives off the volatile fraction and concentrates non-volatile residue in the dish across repeated fills. SCOPE. In scope: mains, USB and tealight-heated oil and oil-and-water evaporators sold with or without a starter oil charge, and the reservoir dish as part of the article. The oil sold separately routes additionally to the refill-materials row. Out of scope: unheated ultrasonic and venturi units, which route to the nebula-diffusers row, and clinical or therapeutic nebulisers regulated as medical devices. The RoHS companion instrument binds the mains, USB and battery variants only, not a purely tealight-heated ceramic burner. COMPONENTS SAMPLED. The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the oil charge; the water or carrier where used; the ceramic, glass, stone or metal reservoir dish and its glaze, frit or coating; the heater element or tealight housing; the printed circuit assembly and solder joints on powered variants; the mains adaptor, USB port or cells; and the moulded or metal housing with its finish. BASIS, AND WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT MEASURE. The panel is a CONTENT SCREEN on the article and on its refill, expressed in micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material. It is not an inhalation exposure limit, not an emission-rate limit, not a per-actuation or per-hour dose limit, and not an indoor-air concentration limit, and it must not be presented as any of those. No credible sovereign government sets an inhalation exposure limit for these metals in a consumer air product, and HMTc does not manufacture one: no occupational exposure limit and no ambient- or indoor-air guideline is converted into a product ceiling anywhere in this category. Because this form works by heating and evaporation, the content screen is a LOWER BOUND on what the emission path can carry: driving off the volatile fraction concentrates non-volatile metal in the reservoir, wick tip or residue film across repeated use, so residue analysis is mandatory alongside the charge as supplied. ROUTING. Placement in this category follows the taxonomy boundary rules: the primary exposure pathway must be inhalation or ambient-air emission; an essential oil sold as aromatherapy for diffusion routes here, the same oil sold as a topical leave-on skin product routes to Category 13 and sold as a dietary supplement routes to Category 16; and marketing and positioning decide routing where one formulation could serve several functions.
heated-oil-diffusers.audit_exclude_scope: non.inhalable|oral route|cutaneous route|edible cannabis|oral consumption|rectal or vaginal|topical|transdermal|drinking water|water intended|bottled|mineral water|public water systems|jewel|\btoy|infant|baby|toddler|\bfeed\b|fertilis|fertiliz|sewage|biosolid|growing media|cosmetic|makeup|make-up|tattoo|eraser
heated-oil-diffusers.basis_guard_note: Category 22 numeric cells are anchored ONLY in route-scoped inhaled-product content instruments, whose register basis strings are "product as tested" (Colorado, Maryland) and "cannabis or cannabis product" (California). The guard admits exactly those and rejects, by construction, every other basis family the register carries: dietary wet-weight maximum levels (an ingestion basis), food-contact and toy element-migration limits (a leachate basis), RoHS and REACH percent-by-weight restrictions on homogeneous materials, plastics, paints and batteries (an end-of-life materials basis), surface-coating dried-film limits, drinking-water statutory limits (a per-litre basis), cosmetic technically-avoidable trace limits (a dermal basis), colour-additive purity specifications, feed 12-percent-moisture bases, and the candlewick prohibition threshold, which is expressed on the mass of the metal in the wick core and not on any product. A number in the wrong basis is not a maximum level for this product form and must never anchor a row here.

read_across.label: read-across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division route-scoped maximum for inhaled product and metered-dose nasal spray (500 ug/kg), corroborated at the identical value by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products
read_across.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a lead content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 500 ug/kg, from Colorado (co2022 inhaled/nasal row). California DCC section 15723 independently sets the identical 0.5 ug/g for inhalable products (us_ca_dcc_2026_pb_inhalable_cannabis_0_5ugg), so two sub-national regulators converge on this value. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: Maryland inhalation route 1000 ug/kg, Massachusetts all-uses protocol 500 ug/kg (equal but route-unspecific), Nevada 1200 ug/kg, Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 5000 ug/kg. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the oil charge as supplied or as specified for use, plus the residue film recovered from the reservoir dish by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. DISPOSITION OF THE ADDITIONAL ANALYSES THIS CELL MANDATES. This cell requires two analyses beyond the published test, and each carries a criterion and a lot consequence, so that no mandatory analysis on this row is an obligation without an outcome. COMPONENT RESULTS, THE FIRST ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The published ceiling of 500 ug/kg governs the emitting material and is NOT transferred to a component's bulk content: a metal reservoir dish, a ceramic glaze or frit, a heater element, a solder joint, a mains adaptor or USB port, or a metal housing finish is or may be substantially metal, metal-plated, metal-glazed or metal-pigmented by construction, and reading an emitting-material value against a structural component's bulk content would be exactly the basis conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent, failing every compliant article for a metal that never enters the air. Every component result is instead dispositioned in three ordered branches, and no component result is left outside them. (a) WHERE A SOVEREIGN INSTRUMENT REACHES THE COMPONENT AND THIS ANALYTE, that instrument is the criterion. The instruments that reach this row's components for lead are: EU Directive 2011/65/EU (RoHS) restricts lead to 1,000,000 ug/kg of any homogeneous material of electrical and electronic equipment (register row eu_rohs_2011_pb_homogeneous_materials_1000000), and this row's powered sub-assembly is such equipment, so its printed circuit assembly, solder joints, heater or drive element, plated contacts, pins and connectors, and moulded housing are each tested as separate homogeneous materials against that value. Further, Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries restricts lead to 100,000 ug/kg of a portable battery by weight (register row eu_batteries_2023_pb_portable_batteries_100000), and it governs any primary or rechargeable cell supplied with the article, tested on the cell as a whole. Each is applied in its own basis at its own threshold, on the component it actually governs, and an exceedance blocks certification of the lot outright irrespective of the emitting-material result. None of these article-and-component values is ever republished as this row's emitting-material limit, because each is three to four orders of magnitude looser and republishing one would misrepresent a component prohibition as a product permission. (b) WHERE THE COMPONENT IS IN THE EMISSION PATH (the reservoir dish with its glaze, frit or coating, and the heated surface the charge stands on), the criterion is the published ceiling itself, applied where its basis makes it meaningful: the test is performed on emitting material sampled from the finished, filled and assembled article rather than from a pre-fill bulk batch, at the end of the declared shelf life or after the declared maximum heated run, whichever is the more demanding, so that any lead transferred out of an emission-path component into the emitting material is carried into the published result rather than escaping it. An emitting-material result at or above 500 ug/kg fails the lot. A rising component result while the emitting material stays below the ceiling does not by itself fail the lot and falls to branch (c). (c) OTHERWISE, for a component outside the emission path that no sovereign instrument reaches for lead, the component result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule, in the same terms this row's control cells already use: the result is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the oil and fragrance supplier, the reservoir and glaze maker, the heater-element maker, the electronics contract manufacturer on powered variants and the housing finisher; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row. No component ceiling is invented in branch (c), because no credible sovereign government publishes a lead content maximum for these components in this product form, and an occupational exposure limit, an indoor-air guideline and an ambient-air standard are none of them converted into one. RESERVOIR RESIDUE FILM, THE SECOND ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The reservoir residue-film analysis is a mass-balance check on the published test, not a second ceiling, because the film is emitting material that has concentrated in place after its volatile mass has evaporated, so a concentration expressed per kilogram of film carries a denominator far smaller than the published basis and is not comparable to it. It is dispositioned in three steps, so that it too carries an outcome. First, the published ceiling of 500 ug/kg governs certification on the emitting material as sampled above: an emitting-material result at or above 500 ug/kg fails the lot, whatever the reservoir residue-film analysis shows. Second, the result is reconciled to the published basis and the reconciled total is what the published value is applied to: the measured film concentration is multiplied by the recovered film mass and divided by the mass of charge run through the reservoir, to give the element recovered from the film per kilogram of charge; where that figure does not exceed the sealed charge's own content, the film is the charge's own non-volatile fraction concentrated in place and no reservoir contribution is demonstrated, while any excess over the sealed charge's content beyond the combined expanded uncertainty of the two determinations is element the charge has picked up from the reservoir dish, its glaze, frit or coating, and that excess is added to the sealed charge's content to give the total presented to the heated surface and through it to the air; a reconciled total at or above 500 ug/kg fails the lot even where the sealed charge on its own was compliant, because the element the charge picks up on its way to the air is element the user inhales; and a pick-up contribution that the manufacturer cannot attribute to a controlled source blocks certification until the contributing component is remediated or substituted. Where the recovered mass cannot be captured and weighed to the precision this comparison requires, the lot is held, re-sampled from a fresh sealed charge and re-tested, and a determination that still cannot be closed fails the lot. Third, the result itself is dispositioned under the control-and-escalation rule stated above, with CAPA and raw-material traceback on an unexplained step change and a block on certification where an uncontrolled source is confirmed. No residue ceiling, emission-rate limit, per-actuation dose limit or indoor-air concentration limit is published for this row, because no credible sovereign government sets one for any product in this category, and none is manufactured from an occupational exposure limit or an ambient-air guideline.
