control.rationale: No government sets an inorganic-arsenic content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. Every route-scoped inhaled-product instrument regulates arsenic as the unspeciated total: Colorado, California, Maryland, Massachusetts, Nevada and Israel all publish total arsenic and none of them speciates, so there is no inorganic-arsenic cell anywhere to read across from. The article and component instruments checked were EU RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU Annex II (lead, cadmium, total mercury and hexavalent chromium in the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment), the EU Batteries Regulation Annex I (mercury, cadmium and lead in batteries), REACH Annex XVII entry 23 (cadmium in synthetic polymers, paint and painted articles), REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin expressed as tin in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public), REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and hexavalent chromium in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles), REACH Annex XVII entry 63 paragraph 7 (lead in mouthable articles), Canada SOR/2016-193 (lead and mercury in surface coating materials), Canada SOR/2018-83 (lead in accessible parts of children's products), Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892 (lead and cadmium in listed covered consumer products), and the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 with EN 71-3 (element migration from toy materials). Every one of them governs a component of an article in a different basis, and none of them is a content maximum for the material a home-air product puts into the breathing zone. The cosmetic content instruments checked and rejected on route were Germany BVL 2017 (technically avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics), Health Canada's cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits, the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive contaminant guideline v3 (2019), Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9, China's 2015 Cosmetics Safety and Technical Standards, India's Cosmetics Rules 2020, Indonesia BPOM 16/2024, Malaysia NPRA, the New Zealand Cosmetic Products Group Standard, Kenya KS 2937:2021, Taiwan's 2024 prohibited-ingredient residual limits, EAEU TR CU 009/2011, and the Hong Kong Mercury Control Ordinance cosmetics provision. All of them are content limits for products applied to the human body on a dermal or mucosal basis. A home-air product is not applied to the body, so none of them is route-applicable. A NOT-MATERIAL determination is deliberately rejected rather than adopted for convenience, because inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction and it is genuinely material in this row. Inorganic arsenic is material here: dried botanical material accumulates soil and irrigation-water arsenic predominantly in inorganic form, and no washing or drying step removes it. The cell is therefore a control: testing is mandatory, the species is bounded by identity below the published total-arsenic ceiling of 200 ug/kg, and no number is invented. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
control.reference_method: Total arsenic on every certified lot of the dried botanical mass with its applied oil and dye, homogenised across the retail unit, with the sachet material analysed as a separate component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the ArCl interference. Reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS is ordered whenever the total-arsenic screen reaches half the published total-arsenic ceiling (100 ug/kg), and unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier of mineral filler, pigment, glaze, frit, clay, charcoal, joss powder, hydrocolloid or dried botanical material. Component-level sampling covers the dried botanical mix (petals, leaves, bark, cones, pods, husks, wood shavings, citrus peel); any decorative mineral, shell, coral or other marine element; the fragrance oil and fixative; the dye or colour wash; and the fabric, paper or mesh sachet, its thread and any metal or plastic closure or hanging hardware. Because inorganic arsenic is a fraction of total arsenic, a lot in which inorganic arsenic alone reaches 200 ug/kg also fails the published total-arsenic ceiling. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. control.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel screen number in this programme; it is the toxic species reached by reflex speciation from total chromium. The cell is a control with reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition. The companion instrument recorded on this cell is REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12, which caps hexavalent chromium at 1 mg/kg after extraction in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles. It is the strictest article-level hexavalent-chromium value on the whole register and it is the nearest textile instrument to a fabric sachet, but its scope is clothing and skin-contact textiles and it does not reach a sachet bag; it is recorded as context for the fabric component only and is not this cell's ceiling.
control.reference_method: Total chromium on every certified lot of the dried botanical mass with its applied oil and dye, homogenised across the retail unit, with the sachet material analysed as a separate component by digestion and ICP-MS, read against the published total-chromium SCREEN of 600 ug/kg. control.rationale: No government sets a methylmercury content limit for any air-care product, and every methylmercury instrument on the register is scoped to fish and other aquatic animals at values far above the 100 ug/kg total-mercury ceiling this row already carries, so no read-across from them would bind anything: methylmercury is a component of total mercury and cannot exceed it. This row admits marine-derived and wild-harvested natural material - ambergris and other marine-animal-derived perfumery fixatives in incense, dried seaweed, shell, coral and other marine decorative elements in potpourri, and undetermined natural inputs on the residual row - so a categorical claim that no methylation pathway exists would be false for part of the row and would fail the not-material substantiation gate. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the botanical grower and consolidator by country and region of origin, fragrance house, dye supplier and the sachet-fabric supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

potpourri-sachets.material: the dried botanical mass with its applied fragrance oil, fixative and dye, evaporating passively through a fabric, paper or mesh sachet
potpourri-sachets.components: The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the dried botanical mix (petals, leaves, bark, cones, pods, husks, wood shavings, citrus peel); any decorative mineral, shell, coral or other marine element; the fragrance oil and fixative; the dye or colour wash; and the fabric, paper or mesh sachet, its thread and any metal or plastic closure or hanging hardware. Every listed component is sampled and tested as a distinct component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, and hexavalent-chromium reflex speciation on a component follows the reference method published on this row's Cr-VI cell. EMISSION PATH. The components in the emission path, which branch (b) of every numeric cell's disposition governs, are the dried botanical mass with its applied oil and dye, any decorative mineral, shell, coral or other marine element in contact with it, and the fabric, paper or mesh through which the fragrance passes. Every component result carries a criterion and a lot consequence under the three ordered branches published on each numeric cell: a sovereign instrument that reaches the component and the analyte governs it in its own basis and an exceedance blocks certification; an emission-path component is governed through the published value applied to emitting material sampled from the finished assembled article; and any remaining component result is held to ALARA against demonstrated process capability, with CAPA, raw-material traceback and a block on certification where an uncontrolled source is confirmed. No component ceiling is invented.

vacuum-cleaner-fragrance-additives.name: Vacuum cleaner fragrance additives
vacuum-cleaner-fragrance-additives.native_basis_label: as sold, micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material (the fragrance concentrate, wax, gel, botanical mass or refill charge that is aerosolised, evaporated or combusted), with component-level screening of the article's non-emitting parts; a content screen on the article and its refill, never an emission rate, a per-actuation dose or an indoor-air concentration
vacuum-cleaner-fragrance-additives.scope_note: FORM AND EMISSION MECHANISM. A granule, powder, bead, disc or impregnated pad is placed in the bag, canister, filter housing or a dedicated holder, and the appliance's own airflow strips fragrance from it and discharges it through the exhaust. The exhaust of a domestic vacuum cleaner is a high-velocity jet directed into the room at floor level, so the additive is dispersed by a mechanism its manufacturer neither controls nor filters, and any friable carrier can be carried over as particulate. SCOPE. In scope: granules, powders, beads, discs, tablets, pads and impregnated strips sold to scent the exhaust of a domestic vacuum cleaner, together with any sachet or dispenser. Out of scope: carpet deodorising powders applied to the floor and vacuumed up, whose primary exposure is deposition and contact rather than exhaust emission, vacuum bags and filters with no fragrance claim, and antimicrobial or biocidal filter treatments. COMPONENTS SAMPLED. The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate (mineral, zeolite, cellulose, starch or polymer); the fragrance load; the dye; any anti-caking, free-flow or fixative agent; and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body. BASIS, AND WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT MEASURE. The panel is a CONTENT SCREEN on the article and on its refill, expressed in micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material. It is not an inhalation exposure limit, not an emission-rate limit, not a per-actuation or per-hour dose limit, and not an indoor-air concentration limit, and it must not be presented as any of those. No credible sovereign government sets an inhalation exposure limit for these metals in a consumer air product, and HMTc does not manufacture one: no occupational exposure limit and no ambient- or indoor-air guideline is converted into a product ceiling anywhere in this category. Because this form works by passive evaporation at room temperature, the emitting mass concentrates its non-volatile content as it depletes, so a result on a fresh unit is a lower bound on the concentration present in the same unit at end of life. ROUTING. Placement in this category follows the taxonomy boundary rules: the primary exposure pathway must be inhalation or ambient-air emission; an essential oil sold as aromatherapy for diffusion routes here, the same oil sold as a topical leave-on skin product routes to Category 13 and sold as a dietary supplement routes to Category 16; and marketing and positioning decide routing where one formulation could serve several functions.
vacuum-cleaner-fragrance-additives.audit_exclude_scope: non.inhalable|oral route|cutaneous route|edible cannabis|oral consumption|rectal or vaginal|topical|transdermal|drinking water|water intended|bottled|mineral water|public water systems|jewel|\btoy|infant|baby|toddler|\bfeed\b|fertilis|fertiliz|sewage|biosolid|growing media|cosmetic|makeup|make-up|tattoo|eraser
vacuum-cleaner-fragrance-additives.basis_guard_note: Category 22 numeric cells are anchored ONLY in route-scoped inhaled-product content instruments, whose register basis strings are "product as tested" (Colorado, Maryland) and "cannabis or cannabis product" (California). The guard admits exactly those and rejects, by construction, every other basis family the register carries: dietary wet-weight maximum levels (an ingestion basis), food-contact and toy element-migration limits (a leachate basis), RoHS and REACH percent-by-weight restrictions on homogeneous materials, plastics, paints and batteries (an end-of-life materials basis), surface-coating dried-film limits, drinking-water statutory limits (a per-litre basis), cosmetic technically-avoidable trace limits (a dermal basis), colour-additive purity specifications, feed 12-percent-moisture bases, and the candlewick prohibition threshold, which is expressed on the mass of the metal in the wick core and not on any product. A number in the wrong basis is not a maximum level for this product form and must never anchor a row here.

read_across.label: read-across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division route-scoped maximum for inhaled product and metered-dose nasal spray (500 ug/kg), corroborated at the identical value by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products
read_across.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a lead content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 500 ug/kg, from Colorado (co2022 inhaled/nasal row). California DCC section 15723 independently sets the identical 0.5 ug/g for inhalable products (us_ca_dcc_2026_pb_inhalable_cannabis_0_5ugg), so two sub-national regulators converge on this value. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: Maryland inhalation route 1000 ug/kg, Massachusetts all-uses protocol 500 ug/kg (equal but route-unspecific), Nevada 1200 ug/kg, Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 5000 ug/kg. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the additive as supplied, homogenised across the retail unit, with the friable fines fraction analysed separately by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. DISPOSITION OF THE ADDITIONAL ANALYSES THIS CELL MANDATES. This cell requires two analyses beyond the published test, and each carries a criterion and a lot consequence, so that no mandatory analysis on this row is an obligation without an outcome. COMPONENT RESULTS, THE FIRST ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The published ceiling of 500 ug/kg governs the emitting material and is NOT transferred to a component's bulk content: a mineral or zeolite carrier substrate, a metal-bearing dye or anti-caking agent, or a pigmented dispenser body is or may be substantially metal, metal-plated, metal-glazed or metal-pigmented by construction, and reading an emitting-material value against a structural component's bulk content would be exactly the basis conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent, failing every compliant article for a metal that never enters the air. Every component result is instead dispositioned in three ordered branches, and no component result is left outside them. (a) WHERE A SOVEREIGN INSTRUMENT REACHES THE COMPONENT AND THIS ANALYTE, that instrument is the criterion. For lead and this row's components, branch (a) is EMPTY, and the instruments checked before saying so are named rather than waved at: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU is scoped to the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment and this row carries no powered sub-assembly; Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries is scoped to batteries and this row contains none; REACH Annex XVII entry 63 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2015/628 (eu_2015_628_pb_mouthable_general_public_articles_0_05pct) reaches only articles supplied to the general public that may be placed in the mouth by children; Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 reaches consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles and does not reach a packaging, sachet or decorative textile that is not worn; the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, the CPSIA surface-coating limit and the Canadian and Australian toy-coating limits reach accessible toy material and toy surface coatings, and none of these articles is a toy; 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) reaches only the metal of a candlewick core and this row has no wick core; the food-contact ceramic, glassware and enamelware instruments reach only articles intended to come into contact with food. Every component result on this row therefore falls to branch (b) or branch (c), and neither leaves a result without a criterion or without a lot consequence. (b) WHERE THE COMPONENT IS IN THE EMISSION PATH (the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate, and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body through which the additive is drawn into the appliance airstream), the criterion is the published ceiling itself, applied where its basis makes it meaningful: the test is performed on emitting material sampled from the finished, filled and assembled article rather than from a pre-fill bulk batch, at the end of the declared shelf life at the declared storage conditions, with the sample homogenised across the retail unit, so that any lead transferred out of an emission-path component into the emitting material is carried into the published result rather than escaping it. An emitting-material result at or above 500 ug/kg fails the lot. A rising component result while the emitting material stays below the ceiling does not by itself fail the lot and falls to branch (c). (c) OTHERWISE, for a component outside the emission path that no sovereign instrument reaches for lead, the component result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule, in the same terms this row's control cells already use: the result is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the carrier-substrate supplier, the fragrance house, the dye supplier, the anti-caking and fixative supplier and the sachet, backing or dispenser converter; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row. No component ceiling is invented in branch (c), because no credible sovereign government publishes a lead content maximum for these components in this product form, and an occupational exposure limit, an indoor-air guideline and an ambient-air standard are none of them converted into one. FRIABLE FINES FRACTION, THE SECOND ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The friable fines fraction is not a separate matrix requiring a separate criterion: it is this row's emitting material in its most respirable form, and the published ceiling of 500 ug/kg applies to it directly and on its own terms. A fines-fraction result at or above 500 ug/kg fails the lot independently of the bulk result, and the bulk result never averages the fines away. Where the fines fraction and the bulk result diverge by more than the combined expanded uncertainty of the two determinations, the lot is held, re-sampled after reconditioning to the declared particle-size distribution and re-tested, and a confirmed enrichment of lead into the respirable fraction that the manufacturer cannot attribute to a controlled source blocks certification. The fines result is otherwise dispositioned under the control-and-escalation rule stated above. No emission-rate limit, per-actuation dose limit or indoor-air concentration limit is published for this row, because no credible sovereign government sets one for any product in this category and none is manufactured from an occupational or ambient-air value.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is not the health-relevant analyte. It is dominated by trivalent chromium, an essential trace element, while the species of concern by the inhalation route is hexavalent chromium, a Group 1 respiratory carcinogen. The Maryland inhalation-route value is a real sovereign number in the right basis and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is the tripwire that triggers hexavalent-chromium speciation (see the Cr-VI cell), not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count. Total chromium is never satisfied by a hexavalent-chromium result and hexavalent chromium is never satisfied by a total-chromium result.
Cr.basis_label: as sold, ug of element per kg of the emitting material (product as tested)

control.rationale: No government sets an inorganic-arsenic content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. Every route-scoped inhaled-product instrument regulates arsenic as the unspeciated total: Colorado, California, Maryland, Massachusetts, Nevada and Israel all publish total arsenic and none of them speciates, so there is no inorganic-arsenic cell anywhere to read across from. The article and component instruments checked were EU RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU Annex II (lead, cadmium, total mercury and hexavalent chromium in the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment), the EU Batteries Regulation Annex I (mercury, cadmium and lead in batteries), REACH Annex XVII entry 23 (cadmium in synthetic polymers, paint and painted articles), REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin expressed as tin in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public), REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and hexavalent chromium in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles), REACH Annex XVII entry 63 paragraph 7 (lead in mouthable articles), Canada SOR/2016-193 (lead and mercury in surface coating materials), Canada SOR/2018-83 (lead in accessible parts of children's products), Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892 (lead and cadmium in listed covered consumer products), and the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 with EN 71-3 (element migration from toy materials). Every one of them governs a component of an article in a different basis, and none of them is a content maximum for the material a home-air product puts into the breathing zone. The cosmetic content instruments checked and rejected on route were Germany BVL 2017 (technically avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics), Health Canada's cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits, the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive contaminant guideline v3 (2019), Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9, China's 2015 Cosmetics Safety and Technical Standards, India's Cosmetics Rules 2020, Indonesia BPOM 16/2024, Malaysia NPRA, the New Zealand Cosmetic Products Group Standard, Kenya KS 2937:2021, Taiwan's 2024 prohibited-ingredient residual limits, EAEU TR CU 009/2011, and the Hong Kong Mercury Control Ordinance cosmetics provision. All of them are content limits for products applied to the human body on a dermal or mucosal basis. A home-air product is not applied to the body, so none of them is route-applicable. A NOT-MATERIAL determination is deliberately rejected rather than adopted for convenience, because inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction and it is genuinely material in this row. Inorganic arsenic is material here: bentonite, zeolite and other mined mineral carriers are a documented inorganic-arsenic-bearing raw material class. The cell is therefore a control: testing is mandatory, the species is bounded by identity below the published total-arsenic ceiling of 200 ug/kg, and no number is invented. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
control.reference_method: Total arsenic on every certified lot of the additive as supplied, homogenised across the retail unit, with the friable fines fraction analysed separately by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the ArCl interference. Reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS is ordered whenever the total-arsenic screen reaches half the published total-arsenic ceiling (100 ug/kg), and unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier of mineral filler, pigment, glaze, frit, clay, charcoal, joss powder, hydrocolloid or dried botanical material. Component-level sampling covers the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate (mineral, zeolite, cellulose, starch or polymer); the fragrance load; the dye; any anti-caking, free-flow or fixative agent; and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body. Because inorganic arsenic is a fraction of total arsenic, a lot in which inorganic arsenic alone reaches 200 ug/kg also fails the published total-arsenic ceiling. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the carrier-mineral or substrate supplier, fragrance house, dye supplier and the anti-caking agent supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

control.rationale: No government sets a nickel content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. Every route-scoped inhaled-product instrument on the register omits nickel entirely, including Maryland's inhalation-route table, which publishes lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium and total chromium but no nickel. The nearest nickel instruments were checked and each fails on basis or on route: the EU Toy Safety Directive nickel values are element MIGRATION limits from toy material under EN 71-3, not content limits; REACH Annex XVII entry 27 governs nickel RELEASE RATE from skin-piercing and prolonged-skin-contact articles; Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9 set nickel content limits for cosmetics on a dermal basis; and EU Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 sets dietary nickel maximum levels on an ingestion basis. No conversion between a migration limit, a release rate, a dermal cosmetic limit and a total-content limit for an inhaled product is defensible, and none is performed. A not-material determination is rejected: Nickel is material here: mineral and zeolite carriers are the most nickel-bearing raw material class in routine use for this form, and a friable mineral carrier in a high-velocity airstream is delivered as inhalable particulate rather than as a vapour. The cell is a control. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
control.reference_method: Nickel on every certified lot of the additive as supplied, homogenised across the retail unit, with the friable fines fraction analysed separately by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with collision/reaction-cell control of the CaO and ArNa interferences. Component-level sampling covers the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate (mineral, zeolite, cellulose, starch or polymer); the fragrance load; the dye; any anti-caking, free-flow or fixative agent; and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body, with every nickel-plated, nickel-alloy and stainless component in the emission path digested and reported separately rather than averaged into the article mass. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the carrier-mineral or substrate supplier, fragrance house, dye supplier and the anti-caking agent supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

control.rationale: No government sets a total-tin content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. The tin instruments on the register were checked and each fails on basis or on scope: the Codex, EU, Hong Kong and Japan canned-food tin maximum levels govern tin dissolved from tinplate INTO A FOOD on a dietary as-consumed basis; the EU Toy Safety Directive tin values are EN 71-3 migration limits from toy material; and REACH Annex XVII entry 20 restricts ORGANOTIN SPECIES expressed as tin in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public, which does directly cover the articles in this row but is a species restriction at 0.1 percent by weight rather than a total-tin content ceiling, and adopting 1,000,000 ug/kg as this row's tin limit would be to publish a number that protects nobody. It is recorded as the companion instrument and enforced as a precondition instead. A not-material determination is rejected: Tin is material here: tin-bearing stabilisers in polymer carriers and disc backings, metallised sachet material, and organotin residues in coated substrates. The cell is a control. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
control.reference_method: Total tin on every certified lot of the additive as supplied, homogenised across the retail unit, with the friable fines fraction analysed separately by microwave-assisted acid digestion in an HCl-containing matrix (tin is readily lost by hydrolysis and precipitation from a nitric-only digest) and ICP-MS. Component-level sampling covers the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate (mineral, zeolite, cellulose, starch or polymer); the fragrance load; the dye; any anti-caking, free-flow or fixative agent; and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body, with tinplate, solder and metallised components reported separately. In addition, REACH Annex XVII entry 20 compliance is a MANDATORY PRECONDITION and is verified by organotin speciation (GC-MS or GC-ICP-MS for dibutyltin, dioctyltin, tributyltin and triphenyltin) on every elastomer, gasket, liner, seal and silicone component: an article supplied to the general public in which organotin expressed as tin exceeds 0.1 percent by weight is unlawful in the European Union and that finding blocks certification outright, independently of the total-tin result. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the carrier-mineral or substrate supplier, fragrance house, dye supplier and the anti-caking agent supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

control.rationale: No government sets an aluminium content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. The aluminium instruments on the register were checked and each fails on basis or on route: the EU Toy Safety Directive aluminium values are EN 71-3 element migration limits from toy material, and the dietary and food-additive aluminium provisions are calibrated to oral intake and oral absorption. Aluminium is also the panel analyte for which route-transfer is least defensible in principle, because a dietary aluminium limit is written against gastrointestinal absorption of well under one percent, which does not describe deposition in the respiratory tract. HMTc states that asymmetry and does NOT convert it into a number: no exposure model, no percentile and no precautionary adjustment produces a value here, and none of the route-scoped inhaled-product instruments publishes aluminium at all. A not-material determination is rejected: Aluminium is material here: zeolite, bentonite, kaolin and talc carriers are aluminosilicates by composition, so the carrier itself is the aluminium source, and it is the fraction most likely to be entrained. The cell is a control. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
control.reference_method: Aluminium on every certified lot of the additive as supplied, homogenised across the retail unit, with the friable fines fraction analysed separately by microwave-assisted acid digestion, using a hydrofluoric or tetrafluoroboric acid step wherever an aluminosilicate mineral phase is present (a nitric-only digest does not liberate aluminium bound in clay, kaolin, talc or zeolite and will under-report it by an order of magnitude), followed by ICP-MS or ICP-OES. Component-level sampling covers the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate (mineral, zeolite, cellulose, starch or polymer); the fragrance load; the dye; any anti-caking, free-flow or fixative agent; and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body, with aluminium primary packaging, foil seals, metallised decoration and aluminosilicate fillers reported separately from the emitting mass. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the carrier-mineral or substrate supplier, fragrance house, dye supplier and the anti-caking agent supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

control.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel screen number in this programme; it is the toxic species reached by reflex speciation from total chromium. No government sets a hexavalent-chromium content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product: Maryland publishes plain total chromium for the inhalation route and does not speciate, and no other route-scoped instrument publishes chromium in any form. The nearest hexavalent-chromium instruments were checked and each fails on basis or on scope: EU RoHS (0.1 percent by weight in the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment), REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 (1 mg/kg after extraction in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles), REACH entry 47 for leather articles, the EU Toy Safety Directive EN 71-3 migration limits, and drinking-water maximum contaminant levels expressed per litre. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other. A not-material determination is rejected: Chromium is material here: mineral carriers carry trivalent chromium and chrome-bearing dyes are used to colour granules; a friable, oxidising, room-temperature carrier releases the mobile hexavalent fraction as particulate. The cell is a control with reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
control.reference_method: Total chromium on every certified lot of the additive as supplied, homogenised across the retail unit, with the friable fines fraction analysed separately by digestion and ICP-MS, read against the published total-chromium SCREEN of 600 ug/kg. Reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation by EPA 3060A alkaline extraction with EPA 6800 isotope-dilution IC-ICP-MS, or by EN 15192, is ordered whenever total chromium reaches half the screen (300 ug/kg), unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier of plated, passivated, glazed, enamelled, mordanted or chrome-pigmented component, and unconditionally on every lot of a combustion or heated form. Component-level sampling covers the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate (mineral, zeolite, cellulose, starch or polymer); the fragrance load; the dye; any anti-caking, free-flow or fixative agent; and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body. DISPOSITION: any hexavalent chromium quantifiable above the method limit of quantitation fails the lot. Inhaled hexavalent chromium is a Group 1 respiratory carcinogen and the programme publishes no permissible level for it; the total-chromium screen is the tripwire, not the ceiling. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the carrier-mineral or substrate supplier, fragrance house, dye supplier and the anti-caking agent supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. This row's emitting material is a manufactured non-marine formulation (the additive as supplied, homogenised across the retail unit, with the friable fines fraction analysed separately) with no methylation pathway, no aquatic trophic transfer and no marine-derived or wild-harvested animal input, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so MeHg is less than or equal to tHg by identity and is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury ceiling of 100 ug/kg. Methylmercury is additionally thermally labile and decomposes well below the temperatures reached in any heated or combustion form in this category, so no thermal pathway creates it either. No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury limit for any air-care product, and no routed occurrence source reports methylmercury in one, which is the speciation-aware condition the not-material integrity gate applies. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling.
not_material.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell, which is determined on every lot by EPA 7473 thermal decomposition/amalgamation atomic absorption or by ICP-MS after closed-vessel digestion. Methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total mercury reaches half the published total-mercury ceiling (50 ug/kg), or where a reformulation introduces any marine-derived, fish-derived or wild-harvested animal raw material, which would additionally require the row to be re-dispositioned from not-material to control.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for an air freshener, evaporator, puff releaser, candle, wax melt, diffuser, incense, potpourri, vacuum fragrance additive or fragrance refill. Every methylmercury instrument on the register is scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, EU Regulation (EU) 2022/617, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Thailand MOPH 414, Vietnam QCVN 8-2, Philippines PNS/BAFS 194, Mexico NOM-242, GSO 193, Trinidad and Tobago). Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically cannot exceed, total mercury, which this row publishes at 100 ug/kg by disclosed read-across from the Colorado inhalation-route maximum.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: Route-scoped inhaled-product instruments: Colorado MED 2022, California DCC section 15723, Maryland Cannabis Administration Rev. 6.0, Massachusetts CCC 2020, Nevada CCB 2020, Israel MoH IMC-GMP 152 - none publishes methylmercury. Article and component instruments: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU, EU Batteries Regulation Annex I, REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23, 63 and 72, Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2018-83, Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892, EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, US 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) - none publishes methylmercury. Cosmetic instruments: Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, ASEAN Cosmetic Directive v3 2019, Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9, China CSAR 2015, India Cosmetics Rules 2020, Indonesia BPOM 16/2024, Malaysia NPRA, New Zealand Group Standard, Kenya KS 2937:2021, Taiwan 2024, EAEU TR CU 009/2011, Hong Kong Mercury Control Ordinance - all regulate total mercury only. Dietary methylmercury instruments are fish-scoped and excluded by applicability.

vacuum-cleaner-fragrance-additives.material: the additive as supplied (carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate with its fragrance load, dye and flow agents), drawn into and dispersed by an appliance airstream
vacuum-cleaner-fragrance-additives.components: The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate (mineral, zeolite, cellulose, starch or polymer); the fragrance load; the dye; any anti-caking, free-flow or fixative agent; and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body. Every listed component is sampled and tested as a distinct component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, and hexavalent-chromium reflex speciation on a component follows the reference method published on this row's Cr-VI cell. Beyond the components, the friable fines fraction is separated and analysed in its own right, the published value applying to it directly. EMISSION PATH. The components in the emission path, which branch (b) of every numeric cell's disposition governs, are the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate, and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body through which the additive is drawn into the appliance airstream. Every component result carries a criterion and a lot consequence under the three ordered branches published on each numeric cell: a sovereign instrument that reaches the component and the analyte governs it in its own basis and an exceedance blocks certification; an emission-path component is governed through the published value applied to emitting material sampled from the finished assembled article; and any remaining component result is held to ALARA against demonstrated process capability, with CAPA, raw-material traceback and a block on certification where an uncontrolled source is confirmed. No component ceiling is invented.

air-product-refill-materials.name: Replacement/refill materials for any dispensing system (oil refills, gel refills, spray refills)
air-product-refill-materials.native_basis_label: as sold, micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material (the fragrance concentrate, wax, gel, botanical mass or refill charge that is aerosolised, evaporated or combusted), with component-level screening of the article's non-emitting parts; a content screen on the article and its refill, never an emission rate, a per-actuation dose or an indoor-air concentration
air-product-refill-materials.scope_note: FORM AND EMISSION MECHANISM. This row is the emitting material itself, sold separately from the device that disperses it: oil vials, gel cups, aerosol cartridges, wick and pad refills, reed replacement sets and bulk concentrate. It carries the highest leverage in the category, because a single refill formulation is dispersed through many device platforms and a metal-bearing raw material in one refill propagates to every device it fits. SCOPE. In scope: every replacement and refill material for a home-air dispensing system, in every physical state: oil vials and bottles, gel cups and cartridges, pressurised aerosol cartridges, wick and pad refills, reed replacement sets, and bulk or concentrate presentations sold for domestic decanting. A refill supplied together with a device is tested on both this row and the device row. Out of scope: device consumables with no fragrance content (filters, batteries, mains adaptors) and industrial or institutional bulk concentrate assessed on an occupational model. COMPONENTS SAMPLED. The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the fragrance concentrate; the carrier solvent or gel matrix; the propellant where present; the dye; the wick, reed or pad where supplied; and the vial, cartridge, cup, closure, gasket, liner and any metal crimp, seal or foil. BASIS, AND WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT MEASURE. The panel is a CONTENT SCREEN on the article and on its refill, expressed in micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material. It is not an inhalation exposure limit, not an emission-rate limit, not a per-actuation or per-hour dose limit, and not an indoor-air concentration limit, and it must not be presented as any of those. No credible sovereign government sets an inhalation exposure limit for these metals in a consumer air product, and HMTc does not manufacture one: no occupational exposure limit and no ambient- or indoor-air guideline is converted into a product ceiling anywhere in this category. Because this form works by passive evaporation at room temperature, the emitting mass concentrates its non-volatile content as it depletes, so a result on a fresh unit is a lower bound on the concentration present in the same unit at end of life. ROUTING. Placement in this category follows the taxonomy boundary rules: the primary exposure pathway must be inhalation or ambient-air emission; an essential oil sold as aromatherapy for diffusion routes here, the same oil sold as a topical leave-on skin product routes to Category 13 and sold as a dietary supplement routes to Category 16; and marketing and positioning decide routing where one formulation could serve several functions.
air-product-refill-materials.audit_exclude_scope: non.inhalable|oral route|cutaneous route|edible cannabis|oral consumption|rectal or vaginal|topical|transdermal|drinking water|water intended|bottled|mineral water|public water systems|jewel|\btoy|infant|baby|toddler|\bfeed\b|fertilis|fertiliz|sewage|biosolid|growing media|cosmetic|makeup|make-up|tattoo|eraser
air-product-refill-materials.basis_guard_note: Category 22 numeric cells are anchored ONLY in route-scoped inhaled-product content instruments, whose register basis strings are "product as tested" (Colorado, Maryland) and "cannabis or cannabis product" (California). The guard admits exactly those and rejects, by construction, every other basis family the register carries: dietary wet-weight maximum levels (an ingestion basis), food-contact and toy element-migration limits (a leachate basis), RoHS and REACH percent-by-weight restrictions on homogeneous materials, plastics, paints and batteries (an end-of-life materials basis), surface-coating dried-film limits, drinking-water statutory limits (a per-litre basis), cosmetic technically-avoidable trace limits (a dermal basis), colour-additive purity specifications, feed 12-percent-moisture bases, and the candlewick prohibition threshold, which is expressed on the mass of the metal in the wick core and not on any product. A number in the wrong basis is not a maximum level for this product form and must never anchor a row here.

read_across.label: read-across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division route-scoped maximum for inhaled product and metered-dose nasal spray (500 ug/kg), corroborated at the identical value by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products
read_across.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a lead content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 500 ug/kg, from Colorado (co2022 inhaled/nasal row). California DCC section 15723 independently sets the identical 0.5 ug/g for inhalable products (us_ca_dcc_2026_pb_inhalable_cannabis_0_5ugg), so two sub-national regulators converge on this value. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: Maryland inhalation route 1000 ug/kg, Massachusetts all-uses protocol 500 ug/kg (equal but route-unspecific), Nevada 1200 ug/kg, Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 5000 ug/kg. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the refill charge as supplied, in the physical state in which it is sold by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. DISPOSITION OF THE ADDITIONAL ANALYSES THIS CELL MANDATES. This cell requires one analysis beyond the published test, and it carries a criterion and a lot consequence, so that no mandatory analysis on this row is an obligation without an outcome. COMPONENT RESULTS, THE FIRST ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The published ceiling of 500 ug/kg governs the emitting material and is NOT transferred to a component's bulk content: a metal crimp, seal or foil, a metallised cartridge or cup, or a pigmented closure is or may be substantially metal, metal-plated, metal-glazed or metal-pigmented by construction, and reading an emitting-material value against a structural component's bulk content would be exactly the basis conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent, failing every compliant article for a metal that never enters the air. Every component result is instead dispositioned in three ordered branches, and no component result is left outside them. (a) WHERE A SOVEREIGN INSTRUMENT REACHES THE COMPONENT AND THIS ANALYTE, that instrument is the criterion. For lead and this row's components, branch (a) is EMPTY, and the instruments checked before saying so are named rather than waved at: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU is scoped to the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment and this row carries no powered sub-assembly; Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries is scoped to batteries and this row contains none; REACH Annex XVII entry 63 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2015/628 (eu_2015_628_pb_mouthable_general_public_articles_0_05pct) reaches only articles supplied to the general public that may be placed in the mouth by children; Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 reaches consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles and does not reach a packaging, sachet or decorative textile that is not worn; the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, the CPSIA surface-coating limit and the Canadian and Australian toy-coating limits reach accessible toy material and toy surface coatings, and none of these articles is a toy; 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) reaches only the metal of a candlewick core and this row has no wick core; the food-contact ceramic, glassware and enamelware instruments reach only articles intended to come into contact with food. Every component result on this row therefore falls to branch (b) or branch (c), and neither leaves a result without a criterion or without a lot consequence.
